problem: Source qualifies John's abuse of his mother: 'he called his mother "old girl," too; sometimes reviled her for her dark skin'. MODERN drops 'too' and 'sometimes', making the reviling unqualified.
new_text: All of John Reed's violent cruelties, all his sisters' cold indifference, all his mother's hostility, all the servants' favoritism—it all churned up in my troubled mind like dark sediment in a stirred well. Why was I always suffering, always put down, always blamed, forever condemned? Why could I never please anyone? Why was it pointless even to try? Eliza, who was stubborn and selfish, was respected. Georgiana, who had a spoiled temper, a sharp spite, and a rude, arrogant manner, was indulged by everyone. Her beauty, her pink cheeks and golden curls, seemed to enchant everyone who saw her, and to buy forgiveness for every fault. No one crossed John, let alone punished him, though he wrung the necks of pigeons, killed baby peacocks, set the dogs on the sheep, stripped the greenhouse vines of their fruit, and broke the buds off the finest plants in the conservatory. He called his mother "old girl," too, sometimes mocked her for her dark skin (which matched his own), blatantly ignored her wishes, and regularly tore and ruined her silk clothes—and he was still "her darling." I dared not make a single mistake. I tried to do everything right. And still I was called naughty and tiresome, sulky and sneaky, from morning to noon and from noon to night.
